trust_decision.summary: The privileged gadget process parses container-controlled ELF .note.stapsdt bytes and trusts the note header sizes and desc length when it slices and allocates, so a bad note panics or over-allocates in the host-side tracer.

landing_point.why: The summary names the USDT note parser. The desc slices desc[:wordSize] and desc[2*wordSize:3*wordSize] are taken with no length check against header.DescSize. Uint64 on a 4-byte word also panics for ELFCLASS32.

fix_sites.entry_point: ebpf operator: gadget program SEC("usdt/<lib>:<provider>:<probe>") -> Tracer.AttachProg / AttachContainer -> attachUprobe -> getUsdtInfo
fix_sites.module_kind: parser (unbounded name/desc allocation from note header sizes)
parser (desc slicing without length check; Uint64 on 4-byte words)

fix_sites.entry_point: shared helper used by getUsdtInfo and parseLdCache (likely the reinterpretBytes rename/replacement)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: pkg/uprobetracer/ldcache_parser.go:142-170 (container /etc/ld.so.cache parser, same package, same helpers readFromBytes/readStringFromBytes)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The advisory is about the USDT note parser in a crafted ELF and says no shipped gadget is affected. The ld.so.cache parser is a different file format and runs for ordinary uprobes in shipped gadgets, so it looks like a separate feature.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate USDT notes must still resolve: 32-bit and 64-bit word sizes, a zero semaphore (no vaddr translation), non-stapsdt notes skipped with continue, 4-byte name/desc padding. For ld.so.cache: the format-1 header followed by an embedded format-2 cache, plus format-2-only files. An over-broad fix that rejects unknown notes or format-1 files breaks attachment.

O6_input_shapes: huge NameSize/DescSize (allocation before the read fails)
provider/probe strings unterminated or starting past desc end

O8_uncovered_routes.route: ld.so.cache parser slices the container file header before any length check (file shorter than the header string panics).
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Not the USDT note parser, and it is reached by shipped library-name uprobe gadgets (e.g. gadgets/profile_cuda/program.bpf.c:159), which the advisory says are unaffected.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: readCacheFormat2 compares data[:len(cache2Header)] with no length check (reached directly when the format-1 header is absent).
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Same as above; it looks like a separate legacy loader-cache format.

O8_uncovered_routes.route: uint32 offset arithmetic (i*entrySize, ldStringsOffset + entry.Key) can wrap, so the bounds check at :89/:123 passes with a wrapped offset.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The bounds check is already present, so it looks hardened.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A hand-rolled .symtab / build-id note reader in the symbolizer, instead of stdlib elfFile.Symbols(), with unchecked lengths.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The symbolizer already opens container ELF files from the host process; a maintainer adding build-id or debuglink lookup would plausibly hand-parse notes like usdt.go does.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A .stapsdt.base / semaphore address translation that indexes Progs data directly.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The USDT semaphore handling already does vaddr->offset math on attacker-controlled addresses.

O9_family: CWE-20 improper input validation in a binary-format parser (out-of-range slice / unbounded allocation -> panic in privileged daemon)

O10_build.toolchain: Go (version per go.mod), standard go test
O10_build.project_tests: None for pkg/uprobetracer at the pinned commit (only bytes.go, ldcache_parser.go, tracer.go, usdt.go). getUsdtInfo and parseLdCache-style parsing are pure functions that can be unit-tested on crafted byte files without eBPF; parseLdCache itself reads via secureopen.ReadFileInContainer (needs a pid).

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add len(desc) >= 3*wordSize before the Uint64 slices in getUsdtInfo, leaving the 32-bit Uint64 bug, the unbounded make(), and the ld.so.cache parser untouched.
